selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does Allah do to the earth with His command?
questions.answer: He gives the earth life again.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the “single cry” lead to?
questions.answer: It leads to everyone being brought forward before Allah.

questions.question: Which two groups of people are clearly named as being gathered?
questions.answer: Human beings and jinn.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about how long resurrection and gathering will take?
questions.answer: It will happen extremely quickly, even faster than a blink.

questions.question: What does the statement about creating and raising all people “like one soul” mean?
questions.answer: It means all of them are just as easy for Allah as one single being.

questions.question: Besides humans and jinn, what other creatures are mentioned as being gathered?
questions.answer: Animals, spirit beings, and angels.

questions.question: Where will they be brought together?
questions.answer: To the place of the great gathering and the great weighing.

questions.question: What important idea is taught by saying one matter does not distract from another?
questions.answer: Allah can handle everything at once without any difficulty.

questions.question: What is one main idea of this whole passage?
questions.answer: Resurrection for all creatures is easy and quick for Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention more than one Qur’anic verse?
questions.answer: To support the message that resurrection is certain, easy, and fast by Allah’s command.

questions.question: What big event is being described in this passage?
questions.answer: The rising again of creation and the final gathering.

questions.question: How is the earth’s return to life connected to Allah in the passage?
questions.answer: It happens by His creative command.

questions.question: What picture is used to show how suddenly the final gathering will happen?
questions.answer: The picture of a single call or command.

questions.question: What comparison is used to show the speed of the Hour?
questions.answer: It is compared to the quickness of blinking.

questions.question: What lesson should a student understand from the phrase about one soul?
questions.answer: Allah does not find many people harder than one person.

questions.question: Who are included in the great assembly according to the passage?
questions.answer: People, jinn, animals, spirit beings, and angels.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s power when many different beings are gathered together?
questions.answer: Gathering all of them is easy for His power.

questions.question: What does “one concern does not interfere with another” tell us about Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: Nothing slows Him down or gets in the way of another action.

questions.question: Is the passage teaching weakness or complete ability about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It teaches complete ability.

questions.question: Why would this passage give hope and certainty to a believer?
questions.answer: It shows that resurrection is fully under Allah’s control and will surely happen.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to the earth by Allah’s command?
questions.answer: It is revived after being lifeless.

questions.question: What happens after the single cry mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: All are brought near and made present.

questions.question: Does the passage limit resurrection to only humans? Explain.
questions.answer: No. It also includes jinn, animals, spirit beings, and angels.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the speed of the Hour compared with normal human actions?
questions.answer: It says it is faster than something as quick as blinking.
